## Week 8: additivity vs interactions, and ensembles

How some flexible fits are built. An additive model fitted one curve at a time, each to what the others leave; its one-input plots, which are partial dependence plots; how additivity can be importantly wrong when the truth has interactions, and how a correct additive fit can still answer the wrong causal question. A tree built one greedy split at a time, then pruned. Bagging and random forests: the variance of an average of correlated trees, and the out-of-bag error. Boosting as approximate gradient descent, one small tree at a time. Partial dependence for other models, and feature importance, come later in the course. Data: IMDb films ([data note](data/movies.html)).

**Reading**

- ISLR Chapter 8 (Tree-Based Methods), section 8.1, pp. 327–340, all of it this time: regression trees again, pruning, classification trees, trees against linear models.
- ISLR Chapter 8, sections 8.2.1–8.2.3, pp. 340–348: bagging (with out-of-bag error and variable importance measures), random forests, boosting. Section 8.2.4, Bayesian additive regression trees, is not part of the course.
- ISLR Chapter 7, section 7.7.1, pp. 307–310, re-read: fitting an additive model one predictor at a time (backfitting).

Optional, deeper: ESL section 9.1.1, pp. 297–299 (the backfitting algorithm); sections 10.10–10.12 (gradient boosting, tree size, regularization).

**Lecture:** [slides](weeks/08-additive/slides/08-1-ensembles.html)

**Seminar:** [notebook](weeks/08-additive/notebooks/notebook8.html) ([.qmd](https://ml4ds.com/weeks/08-additive/notebooks/notebook8.qmd){download="notebook8.qmd"}). Before the seminar, do exercises 1 and 2 at the top of the notebook (the variance of an average of correlated trees, with the slides closed, and one boosting step by hand); the seminar's problems are variations on them, with one more on what a larger search costs. Then tuning a random forest and boosted trees on the films ([data note](data/movies.html)): one knob at a time against all of them together, how the size of the search changes what the best score means, and the test films opened once.
